convention: Every number a turn settles comes from a mechanic this game names, run by `akasha game settle --game game/the-tower --turn <n> --mechanic <address> --reading <json> --dice 2d10`. The command rolls the dice itself from the hash of the row before, runs the mechanic, appends the run to mechanicRuns and answers the numbers, so no roll is asked for twice and none is thumbed. The GM reads the relevant attribute and the telegraphed difficulty from the fiction BEFORE the call and hands them in as the reading; the die is only the luck. A non-combat check is `game-mechanic/attribute-check --reading '{"attribute":11,"difficulty":24,"intent":4}'`. A strike is `game-mechanic/attack-resolution --reading '{"attackPower":33.5,"defense":11,"baseDamage":14,"gate":0.3,"intent":3}' --bonuses '[{"from":"Ember Channel","by":1}]'`, where `gate` is the multiplier the encounter's page names among its gates for the read the player made, and defaults to 1. Both answer a band (fumble -> fail, crit -> clean success, hit -> success, graze -> success-at-a-cost, miss -> fail), a margin and a damage. The numbers fix the MAGNITUDE; the GM adjudicates the concrete outcome and its cost against the fiction. Scope contract (see gmContext policy resolution-scope): ROUTINE / low-stakes non-combat is GM judgment and needs no call; the lethal-vs-routine lane is the GM's per-check judgment call, and once a check is lethal or contested the mechanic settles it. Loop-dark: a run is the GM's to read, never a client payload; the first result remains unless the fiction itself changed.
